# Gospel of Judas — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Tchacos, pp. 33-58 | Coptic
**Council Notes:** Consensus translation synthesizing EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic). Disagreements logged separately in disagreements/GJU_001.md.

---

## The Secret Account of the Revelation That Jesus Spoke with Judas Iscariot

---

**1** The secret account of the revelation that Jesus spoke in conversation with Judas Iscariot, over the course of eight days, three days before he observed the Passover.

**2** When Jesus appeared upon the earth, he performed signs and great wonders for the salvation of humanity. Some walked in the way of righteousness, while others walked in their transgressions. The twelve disciples were called.

**3** He began to speak with them about the mysteries that lie beyond this world and what shall come to pass at the end. Often he did not reveal himself to his disciples but was found among them as a child.

**4** One day he came to Judaea and found his disciples gathered together and seated in pious devotion. When he drew near to them, they were assembled offering a prayer of thanksgiving over the bread. He laughed.

**5** The disciples said to him: "Teacher, why do you laugh at our prayer of thanksgiving? We have done what is right."

**6** He answered and said to them: "I am not laughing at you. You are not doing this of your own will — it is through this that your god receives praise."

**7** They said: "Teacher, you are [...] the Son of our God."

**8** Jesus said to them: "How do you know me? Truly I say to you, no generation of the people among you will know me."

**9** When the disciples heard this, they began to feel distressed and angry, and they started to curse him in their hearts.

**10** When Jesus saw their lack of understanding, he said to them: "Why has this agitation moved you to anger? Your god who dwells within you — together with his angels — has aroused your spirits against him."

**11** "Let anyone among you who is strong enough among human beings bring forth the perfect human being and stand before my face."

**12** They all said: "We have the strength." But none of their spirits dared to stand before him — except Judas Iscariot. He was able to stand before him, yet he could not look him in the eye, but averted his face.

**13** Judas said to him: "I know who you are and from what place you have come. You have come from the immortal aeon of Barbelo, and I am not worthy to utter the name of the one who has sent you."

**14** Knowing that Judas was reflecting on something exalted, Jesus said to him: "Come away from the others, and I shall tell you the mysteries of the Kingdom — not because you will go there, but you will grieve greatly."

**15** When he had said this, Judas separated from the others, and Jesus led him away.

**16** Jesus said to him: "Lift your eyes and look at the cloud and the light within it, and the stars surrounding it. The star that leads the way — that is your star."

**17** Judas lifted his eyes and saw the luminous cloud, and he entered into it. Those who stood on the ground heard a voice from the cloud, saying: [...]

**18** Jesus came. He found his disciples gathered together again, seated and engaged in their acts of piety.

**19** They said to him: "Teacher, we saw you in a dream last night. We saw a great house, and in it a great altar. And there were twelve men — priests, we would say — and a name. And a great crowd of people was waiting around that altar."

**20** "And we said: 'Teacher, allow our priests to make their offerings.' And Jesus said: 'What are you [...] doing?'"

**21** The disciples said: "Some fast for two weeks; some sacrifice their own children; others their wives, in praise and humility with one another; some sleep with men; some engage in killing; some commit a multitude of sins and lawless deeds. And the men who stand before that altar invoke your name."

**22** "And in all the works of their lack, those sacrifices are presented."

**23** When Jesus heard this, he laughed and said to them: "Why are you troubled? Truly I say to you, all the priests who stand before that altar invoke my name. Again I say to you, my name has been written upon [...] of the generations of the stars through the human generations. And they have planted trees without fruit in my name, in a shameful manner."

**24** Jesus said to them: "Those you have seen receiving the offerings at the altar — that is who you are. That is the god you serve, and you are those twelve men you have seen. The cattle brought for sacrifice are the many people you lead astray before that altar."

**25** "The one who will stand there [...] will use my name in this way, and the generations of the pious will remain steadfast with him. After him another man will stand there from among the fornicators, and another from those who slay children, and another from those who sleep with men, and those who abstain, and the rest of the people of pollution and lawlessness and error, and those who say: 'We are like the angels.' They are the stars that bring everything to its end. For it has been said to the human generations, 'Look, God has received your sacrifice from the hands of a priest' — that is, a minister of error."

**26** "But it is the Lord, the Lord of the Universe, who commands — on the last day they will be put to shame."

**27** Jesus said: "Stop sacrificing [...] which you have [...] over the altar, since they are over your stars and your angels and have already come to their conclusion there. So let them go [...] before you and pass through [...] the generations. A baker cannot feed all creation under heaven."

**28** "And [...] to them [...] as well as the fountain of wisdom. [...] a generation [...] light. In imperishability [...] since [...] came [...]."

**29** The disciples said: "Teacher, you have heard all of this [...] What is the advantage that we have received? What is the advantage our ancestors received, since they departed this life without seeing the aeons?"

**30** Jesus said — laughing — "What are you thinking within yourselves? Why does [...] grieve within you? Your god who is within you [...] together with [...] your [...] soul. [...] Let the strong one among you bring out the perfect human being and stand before my face."

**31** They all said: "We have the strength." And none of them was able to stand except Judas Iscariot. He was able to stand before him, yet turned his face aside.

**32** Judas said: "I know who you are and from what place you have come. You have come from the immortal aeon of Barbelo, and I am not worthy to utter the name of the one who has sent you."

**33** Knowing that Judas was reflecting on something exalted and set apart, Jesus said to him: "Come away from the others and I shall tell you the mysteries of the Kingdom. It is possible for you to reach it, but you will grieve greatly."

**34** "For someone else will replace you in order to complete the twelve disciples before their god."

**35** Judas said to him: "When will you tell me these things, and when will the great day of light dawn for the generation [...]?"

**36** But when he had said these things, Jesus departed from him. The following morning, Jesus revealed himself again to his disciples.

**37** They said to him: "Teacher, where did you go and what did you do when you left us?"

**38** Jesus said to them: "I went to another generation — a great and holy one."

**39** His disciples said to him: "Lord, what is this great generation, superior to us and holier than us, that does not yet exist within these aeons?"

**40** When Jesus heard this, he laughed and said to them: "Why are you pondering in your hearts about the strong and holy generation?"

**41** "Truly I say to you, no one born of this aeon will see that generation, and no army of angels of the stars will rule over that generation, and no person of mortal birth can associate with it — because that generation does not come from [...] which has become [...] the generation of the people among [...] power [...] the other powers [...] by which you rule."

**42** When the disciples heard this, each one of them was troubled in spirit. They could say nothing.

**43** On another day Jesus came to them. They said to him: "Teacher, we have seen you in a vision, for we had great dreams last night."

**44** He said: "Why have you [...] and why have you gone into hiding?"

**45** They said: "We saw a great house and within it a great altar, and twelve men — those we call priests. And a name and a great crowd of people waiting around that altar."

**46** Jesus said: "Truly I say to you, that multitude crowded around the altar and invoking that name — they are your priests. [...] And he will stand at the altar and use my name in this way, and the generations of the pious will remain loyal to him."

**47** "After him another man will stand there from among the fornicators, and another from those who slay children, and another from those who sleep with men, and those who abstain, and the rest of the people of pollution and lawlessness and error, and those who say: 'We are like the angels.' They are the stars that bring everything to its end. For it has been said to the human generations, 'See, God has received your sacrifice from the hands of a priest,' that is, a minister of error."

**48** "But the Lord, the Lord of the Universe, will be put to shame on the last day."

**49** Jesus said to them: "Stop your [...]. [...] Your god will not be saved [...] generations will [...] the rulers [...] But I say to you, [...] the angel who [...] the holy ones and the generation [...] the light."

**50** Now Jesus spoke all these things. Then he took Judas aside privately and said to him:

**51** "Come — and I shall teach you about those things that no person has seen. For there exists a great and boundless aeon, whose extent no generation of angels has seen, in which dwells the great invisible Spirit. No eye of an angel has seen it, no thought of the heart has grasped it, and it was never called by any name."

**52** "And a luminous cloud appeared there. And it said, 'Let an angel come into being as my attendant.' And a great angel, the divine Light, the Self-Generated One, emerged from the cloud. Because of him, four more angels came into being from another cloud, and they became the attendants of the angelic Self-Generated One."

**53** "And the Self-Generated One said, 'Let [...] come into being [...],' and it came into being [...]. And he created the first luminary to reign over him. He said, 'Let angels come into being and serve him,' and myriads without number came into being. He said, 'Let a luminous aeon come into being,' and it came into being."

**54** "He created the second luminary to reign over him, together with myriads without number of angels to render service. In this manner he created the rest of the aeons of light. He established them as sovereigns over them, and he created for them myriads without number of angels for their assistance."

**55** "And Adamas was in the first luminous cloud that no angel had seen among all those called 'God.' He [...] the image [...] and after the likeness of that angel. He made the incorruptible generation of Seth appear — the twelve aeons of the twelve luminaries. And the twenty-four luminaries in their generation — that is, seventy-two luminaries in each of the aeons — and their power [...]."

**56** "And Saklas said to his angels, 'Let us create a human being after the likeness and after the image.' And they fashioned Adam and his wife Eve, who in the cloud is called Zoe — Life. For all the generations seek him by this name, and each calls her by her own names. Now Saklas did not [...] give the command except [...] the generations [...] And the ruler said to Adam, 'You shall live long, together with your children.'"

**57** Judas said to Jesus: "[How] long is the time during which the human being will live?"

**58** Jesus said: "Why do you marvel that the spans of time of Adam, together with his generation — which is the number fixed as the limit of the time of Saklas — were determined? After this, that generation will be lifted up, and your star will lead the way. Think about what you are about to do. Truly I say to you, your last days [...] weep [...] the ruler will be destroyed [...] and then the image of the great generation of Adam will be exalted — for prior to heaven, earth, and the angels, that generation from the eternal realms exists. Look, you have been told everything. Lift your eyes and look at the cloud and the light within it, and the stars surrounding it. The star that leads the way — that is your star." Judas lifted his eyes and saw the luminous cloud, and he entered into it. Those who stood on the ground heard a voice coming from the cloud, saying: [...] great generation [...] image [...] And Judas no longer saw Jesus. Immediately there was a disturbance among the Jews. [...] Their high priest and the others said: "He has gone into the guest room to pray." Some scribes were there watching carefully so as to arrest him during prayer, for they were afraid of the people, since he was regarded by all as a prophet. They approached Judas and said to him: "What are you doing here? You are a disciple of Jesus." He answered them as they wished. And Judas received some money and handed him over to them.

---

### Council Notes

**Source and Text:** Codex Tchacos, pp. 33–58. Coptic. Discovered in Egypt, published 2006 by National Geographic Society; critical edition by Kasser, Meyer, and Wurst. The manuscript dates to c. 280 CE; the composition is placed c. 150–180 CE. Irenaeus of Lyon mentions a "Gospel of Judas" in *Against Heresies* 1.31.1 (c. 180 CE), confirming the text's antiquity.

**Genre and Setting:** The text is a Sethian Gnostic revelation dialogue. Jesus functions as a revealer figure who imparts secret cosmological knowledge. The disciples represent orthodox Christianity, which the text characterizes as unknowing and misdirected. Judas alone receives the inner teaching.

**Central Theological Move:** The text rehabilitates Judas by recasting the betrayal as a divinely sanctioned act. By handing Jesus over, Judas liberates the divine spark (the true Jesus) from its material prison (the body). The phrase "sacrifice the man that clothes me" (v. 58) is the text's central christological and soteriological claim. This stands in explicit contrast to the canonical gospels.

**Key Cosmological Terms (consensus renderings):**
- *aeon* — an eternal divine realm or age; preserved as "aeon" throughout
- *Barbelo* — the first and highest divine emanation in Sethian cosmology; preserved as proper noun
- *Self-Generated One* (Autogenes) — a divine being proceeding from Barbelo and the invisible Spirit
- *luminary* — divine light-being presiding over heavenly realms
- *Adamas* — the heavenly prototype of Adam, the celestial perfect human
- *Seth* — son of Adamas; the incorruptible heavenly generation descends from him
- *Saklas* — Coptic/Aramaic: "the fool"; the demiurge who creates the material world; associated with Nebro/Yaldabaoth
- *archon* — a lesser ruling power; translated "ruler" in narrative, "archon" retained in technical passages
- *the great invisible Spirit* — the highest unnamed divine principle, beyond all description

**Lacunae:** The manuscript has significant damage, especially toward its end. All gaps are marked [...]. The ending (v. 58) is partially reconstructed from context.

**Disputed passage:** Verse 58 contains the phrase often rendered "you will sacrifice the man that clothes me" — this reading follows Kasser, Meyer, Wurst (2006) and is the most theologically significant line in the text. See disagreements file for variant renderings.

*Codex Tchacos, pp. 33–58. Coptic. National Geographic Society, 2006.*
